literal: Or perhaps serving as official on outer garrison. Tongdian juan 15 records Yuan Yong's memorial with "ren" (hold office) written as "zheng" (campaign).
idiomatic: "Or perhaps serving as official on outer garrison": Tongdian juan 15, Yuan Yong's memorial, reads ren (hold office) as zheng (campaign).

literal: Commentary: "Campaign official" means an official on campaign; hence it is linked with "outer garrison"; "ren" is suspected corrupt.
idiomatic: Note: "campaign official" denotes an officer in the field, hence pairs with "outer garrison"; ren is likely corrupt.

literal: Zhen Chen memorialized, saying. In various editions "chen" (gem) is everywhere written as "shen" (deep).
idiomatic: "Zhen Chen memorialized, saying": every edition reads chen (gem) as shen (deep).

literal: Commentary: The passage appears in juan 68, Biography of Zhen Chen; "shen" is a graphic corruption and is now corrected.
idiomatic: Note: the passage is in juan 68 (Zhen Chen); shen is a shape corruption and is corrected.

literal: For merit enfeoffed as Duke of Ande County with an open state. In various editions "de" (virtue) is written as "de" (obtain).
idiomatic: "For merit enfeoffed duke of Ande county, open state": editions read de (virtue) as de (obtain).

literal: Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Duan
idiomatic: Per Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Duan

literal: 〈plate 179〉
idiomatic: plate 179

literal: reads "Duke of Ande commandery with an open state."
idiomatic: has "duke of Ande commandery, open state."

literal: Commentary: Juan 106 upper, Monograph on Geography, upper, Ji Province, Ande commandery, states: "Established in the Taihe era, soon merged into Bohai; restored in the Zhongxing era," and the commandery subordinates include Ande county.
idiomatic: Note: Geography monograph juan 106 upper, Ji, Ande commandery: "set up in Taihe, soon merged into Bohai, restored in Zhongxing," with Ande county subordinate.

literal: "An obtain" is clearly a corruption of "Ande"; now corrected.
idiomatic: "An obtain" clearly corrupts "Ande"; the text is emended.

literal: According to the geography monograph, when Yuan Duan received his enfeoffment, this was after the commandery had been merged into Bohai and before the commandery was restored; at the time there was no Ande commandery.
idiomatic: By the geography monograph, Yuan Duan's enfeoffment fell after Ande was merged into Bohai and before the commandery was restored—there was then no Ande commandery.

literal: Though Northern Wei fiefs were all nominal, and before Taihe names were set even more at will and need not match an existing commandery, after Taihe's fixed regulations this situation had already changed somewhat.
idiomatic: Northern Wei fiefs were nominal, and before Taihe titles were coined freely without a matching commandery, but after Taihe's rules that looseness had narrowed.

literal: Since there was no "Ande" commandery, the biography's "county duke" is not necessarily wrong; not changed now.
idiomatic: With no Ande commandery, "county duke" in the life need not be wrong; left unchanged.

literal: At night the guards reported it; Xiang wept several times and died suddenly. Li Ciming says: "'The guards reported it'—the character 'yi' (by/with) is superfluous.
idiomatic: "At night the guards reported it; Xiang wept several times and died suddenly": Li Ciming says the character yi (by/with) in "the guards reported it" is redundant.

literal: Above it already says 'presented the memorial'; one cannot again say 'reported it.'
idiomatic: Above already says "presented the memorial"; "reported it" cannot follow.

literal: Moreover, just when 'reporting it,' the harm to Xiang is not yet spoken—how can it immediately say 'Xiang wept several times and died'?
idiomatic: Besides, at the moment of "reporting it" Xiang's killing is not yet told—how can the next line be "Xiang wept several times and died"?

literal: Beishi
idiomatic: In Beishi

literal: 〈juan 19〉
idiomatic: juan 19

literal: below 'Lan obtained and presented the memorial' says: 'The emperor secretly ordered him killed.'
idiomatic: below "Lan obtained and presented the memorial" reads: "The emperor secretly ordered him killed."

literal: This biography must have dropped a sentence; hence below it says: 'At night the guards heard Xiang weep several times and he died.'
idiomatic: This life must drop a line; hence below: "At night the guards heard Xiang weep several times and he died."

literal: Probably no one knew the manner of his death."
idiomatic: Likely no one knew how he died."

literal: The Xiang Province mobile secretariat Zhen Mi had earlier received the court's order. In various editions the character "mi" (dense) is missing.
idiomatic: "Xiang Province mobile secretariat Zhen Mi had earlier received the court's order": editions omit mi (dense).

literal: Commentary: Below "Zhen" one should not omit the personal name.
idiomatic: Note: after "Zhen" the personal name must not be omitted.

literal: Zizhi tongjian juan 152
idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian, scroll 152

literal: 〈folio 4747〉
idiomatic: folio 4747

literal: reads "Zhen Mi."
idiomatic: has "Zhen Mi."

literal: Zhen Mi as Xiang Province mobile secretariat also appears in juan 68, his basic biography; here "mi" has dropped out and is now supplied accordingly.
idiomatic: Zhen Mi as Xiang mobile secretariat appears in juan 68 (his biography); mi dropped here and is supplied.

literal: Hao's younger brother Xu. In various editions "xu" is written as "zhen" (jade ornament).
idiomatic: "Hao's younger brother Xu": editions read xu as zhen (jade ornament).

literal: Corrected according to Beishi juan 19 and Cefu juan 281
idiomatic: Emended per Beishi juan 19 and Cefu juan 281

literal: 〈folio 3312〉
idiomatic: folio 3312

literal: , Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Xu
idiomatic: ; Muzhi jishi, epitaph of Yuan Xu

literal: 〈plate 184〉
idiomatic: plate 184

literal: Corrected; see collation notes to juan 10.
idiomatic: Emended; see textual notes to juan 10.
